From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>

Date: 2028-03-01T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and qualification

Hi Alex / Priya — great to meet you both on the call today. Thanks for walking through Acme's planned usage patterns. Quick recap + a few asks so we can finalize a proposal: 

Summary from call:
- Expected steady-state: ~200M tokens / month (NLP assistant + summarization flows).
- Peak days: up to 10M tokens/day during product launches.
- Burst behavior: short spikes up to ~5k concurrent requests for 10-60 minutes during launches.
- Latency SLO: 500ms p50 for generation flows; willing to trade slightly higher latency for cost on non-critical paths.

Questions / asks so we size quota / burst policy and overage terms:
1) Confirm target budget range for inference (monthly). You mentioned a ballpark; can you confirm a target $/1M tokens you want to stay near? (helps us recommend quantization / batching profiles).
2) Do you expect 3rd-party integrations (webhooks, background workers) to share the same quota or be billed separately?
3) Any procurement constraints / PO cadence we should align to?
4) Can you share a 30-day example peak day token distribution (if available) — attachment 'acme-maup-estimates.csv' would help.

What we'll propose after you confirm:
- Baseline quota to cover 200M tokens / month.
- Burst cushion for up to 10M/day with automatic short-term burst allowance (subject to throttles) and an option for committed burst buffer for launches.
- Overage terms: tiered per-1M-token overage rates with a discount applied for committed volume; alternative: a soft throttle with email + automated quota increase option.

I'm attaching our current rate card (redwood-rate-card-v2.xlsx) and a draft SOW for estimated ramp (SOW_draft_acme.pdf). If you can confirm the target $/1M and whether integrations are on the same quota by EOD tomorrow, Rafael and I will return pricing & quota options for you to review.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the materials. Quick answers below: 

1) Target budget: we are aiming for $1,800 per 1M tokens as an upper bound today; if we can get to ~$1,400/1M at scale that's ideal.
2) Integrations: external integrations (partner webhooks) will be billed from a separate platform account and should not share the primary quota; internal workers and web UI will share the same quota.
3) Procurement: typical PO / Net30 cadence; legal sometimes asks for limited SLA/credits language.
4) Attached is a peak day export (see acme-maup-estimates.csv) — you can see spikes during launch windows with 2–3 hour elevated traffic.

On bursts: we'd prefer a committed burst cushion for known launches (we can provide advance notice 48–72 hours). For unexpected spikes we'd accept soft-throttles but need a predictable overage rate so our finance team can model cost.

Let Rafael know if you need more granular RPS numbers; happy to have our infra lead hop on a quick call.

Best,
Alex
Head of Product, Acme Corp

Subject: Proposed options — Rate limits & overage for Acme (ACME-2319)

Hi Alex / Priya / Marissa — thanks for the details and the CSV — helpful. Attached is a concise pricing proposal and math. High level: two options as requested.

Option A — Hosted (flex)
- Baseline: 200M tokens / month included.
- Rate-limits: default 600 RPS account-level with route-level soft throttles; burst allowance: up to 10M tokens/day handled via automatic short-term bursting (up to 3x baseline RPS for 60 minutes).
- Overage: $1,950 per 1M tokens for unexpected overage; tiered discounts at 10% for monthly >300M and 20% >500M.
- Quota increase SLA: standard (24–48 hours) for >20% increase; emergency increase (on-call escalation) typically within 4 hours with partner approval.

Option B — Committed (recommended for launches)
- Baseline committed: 200M tokens / month at $1,600 per 1M (committed rate).
- Committed burst buffer: additional 50M tokens/month reserved for launches (pre-approved 48–72h notice). During a pre-authorized launch, we raise the route-level quota and allow bursts up to 5x baseline RPS for up to 3 hours.
- Overage (on top of reserved burst): $1,400 per 1M tokens.
- Support & procurement: Net30 invoices, support plan includes one scheduled launch window per quarter for free quota reallocation.

Examples (invoice impact):
- If Acme exceeds baseline by 10% (20M tokens) on Hosted: 20M / 1M * $1,950 = $39,000 overage.
- On Committed plan, same 20M over baseline would be within reserved burst buffer (no extra charge if pre-authorized) or $1,400/1M => $28,000 if outside reserved buffer.

Attachments: redwood-rate-card-v2.xlsx (updated pricing rows), SOW_draft_acme.pdf (SOW notes), and a sample billing worksheet.

Next steps:
1) Alex — confirm preferred option (A or B) and whether you want committed burst buffer sized differently.
2) If Option B, sign SOW / commit volume and we'll provision reserved burst buffer and set up billing terms.
3) We'll schedule a short tech sync (Camila + your infra) to confirm RPS and routing rules.

Happy to hop on a call to run through the invoice math with your finance team.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
